standard_prerequisites.name: Independence of the Chern class of a bounded finite locally free complex representing a perfect object
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-pre-derived-chern-class, invoked at proof line 9239
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the class c_p of a complex representing Lg^*E well defined on any locally finite type T -> X, which is what allows the construction to be base changed freely.

standard_prerequisites.name: Restriction of bivariant classes and the bivariant character of c_p
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels remark-restriction-bivariant (proof line 9246) and lemma-cap-cp-bivariant (proof line 9248)
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the class obtained after a further base change with the restriction of the earlier one, so that the two restrictions in the envelope descent lemma really coincide.

standard_prerequisites.name: Descent of a bivariant class along an envelope, and the envelope properties of base change and composition
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-envelope-bivariant (proof lines 9253 and 9268), lemma-base-change-envelope and lemma-composition-envelope (proof lines 9266-9267), and definition-envelope (statement, proof line 9217)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the descended bivariant class c_p(E) on X from the class on Y, and gives the uniqueness by applying the same descent lemma to the product envelope Y times_X Y' -> X.

core_obligations: Construct the class on any test scheme: for g : T -> X locally of finite type over which Lg^*E is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules, define c_p(Lg^*E) as the class of that complex, well defined by the independence lemma, and observe that for a further locally finite type h : T' -> T the class of L(g o h)^*E is the restriction of c_p(Lg^*E) to T', using the bivariant character of c_p (proof lines 9230-9248).

Descend along the given envelope: apply the envelope descent lemma to f : Y -> X and the class c' = c_p(Lf^*E), verifying its hypothesis by noting that both restrictions are c_p(Lg^*E) for g = f o p = f o q, where p and q are the two projections from Y times_X Y (proof lines 9250-9258).

Prove independence of the envelope: for a second envelope f' : Y' -> X with the same property, the restrictions of c_p(Lf^*E) and c_p(L(f')^*E) to Y times_X Y' agree, and since Y times_X Y' -> X is again an envelope by base change and composition the uniqueness part of the descent lemma identifies the two candidates (proof lines 9260-9268).
proof_roadmap: Define c_p on every test scheme where E trivialises and check base change (proof lines 9230-9248).
Descend along the given envelope using the equality of the two restrictions (proof lines 9250-9258).
Compare two different envelopes through the product envelope and the uniqueness of descent (proof lines 9260-9268).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces the Chern class, the Chern character and the Chern polynomials of a perfect object E on X as bivariant classes, assuming that after some envelope Y -> X the pullback becomes a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules, and asserts that they are independent of that envelope (statement lines 9212-9227, tag 0GUD). The proof builds the classes on every test scheme, verifies that base change acts by restriction, and then feeds the construction into the descent lemma for bivariant classes along an envelope, checking the hypothesis through the two projections; independence of the envelope is obtained by the same descent applied to the product envelope. The organisation of these descents is the substance, so the claim is H2.
